title: Cardinal Roadside Assistance Holding Rule: One Option per Vehicle
content:
## Rule

Cardinal Roadside Assistance is held per vehicle. A vehicle carries at most one Cardinal Roadside Assistance option, and a customer may add an option to every vehicle scheduled on their policy; there is no cap of its own on the number of options one customer holds. An option can be added to a vehicle only when the vehicle has no active option.

## The rule broken down

| Question | Answer under this rule |
|---|---|
| What is the unit of holding? | The vehicle. Each option belongs to one scheduled vehicle. |
| How many options may one vehicle carry? | At most one. |
| How many options may one customer hold? | One on every scheduled vehicle; the rule sets no separate per-customer limit. |
| When can an option be added to a vehicle? | Only when that vehicle has no active option. |
| Whose word settles whether an active option exists? | The company's own coverage records for that vehicle, checked before the option is added. |

## Points of judgement

- The check is made on the vehicle being added to: the active options of other vehicles in the household do not stand in the way of adding an option to this vehicle.
- An option whose status on the record is removed or nonrenewed is not an active option, so it does not stand in the way of adding an option to that vehicle.

## Hypothetical cases

| Household records | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Three scheduled vehicles; none has an option | Add an option to each of the three | Each may be added: one option per vehicle, no per-customer cap |
| Vehicle A has an active option | Add a second option to vehicle A | Not added: vehicle A already has an active option |
| Vehicle A has an active option; vehicle B has none | Add an option to vehicle B | May be added: vehicle B has no active option |
| Vehicle C's earlier option shows as removed | Add an option to vehicle C | May be added: vehicle C has no active option |

The vehicles in these cases are illustrative.
